timeline.evidenceText: “Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon,
Nebo, and Baal Meon, (their names being changed), and Sibmah. They gave other names to the cities which they built.
They traveled from Almon Diblathaim, and encamped in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo.
“Go up into this mountain of Abarim, to Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, that is across from Jericho; and see the land of Canaan, which I give to the children of Israel for a possession.
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is opposite Jericho. Yahweh showed him all the land of Gilead to Dan,
and Bela the son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Joel, who lived in Aroer, even to Nebo and Baal Meon;
Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Iddo, and Joel, Benaiah.
The men of the other Nebo: fifty-two.
They have gone up to Bayith, and to Dibon, to the high places, to weep. Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba. Baldness is on all of their heads. Every beard is cut off.
Of Moab. Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says:
on Dibon, on Nebo, on Beth Diblathaim,

definitions.short: Nebo , the name of a Babylonian deity, also of a mountain in Moab, and of a place in Palestine
definitions.full: H5015. Nbow I. נְבוֺ proper name, of a location (probably connection, at least for 2 , with (Babylonian) god Nebo, Nabû , compare II. נְבוֺ and Bae Rel. 15. 89, 259 ; yet not certain, Nö ZMG xiii. 1888, 470 compare Arabic the height , etc.): ᵐ5 Ναβαυ ; — 1. a. city in Moab Num 32:3 , 38 (where assigned to Reuben; both J E = נבה MI 14 ) Isa 15:2 ; Jer 48:1 , 22 ; 1Chr 5:8 ; probably on or near Mt. Nebo (see below), compare Buhl Geogr. 266 f. Tristr Moab 338. b. city in Judah , נ ׳בְּנֵי Ezra 2:29 = נ ׳אַנְשֵׁי אַחֵר Neh 7:34 ( the men of the other N. , so distinguished — si אחר vera l., compare Ryle — from a ? or from another נֹב ?), Ezra 10:43 ; — this נבו in Judah perhaps = נֹב 1 q. v. 2 mountain in Moab, where Moses died Num 33:47 ; Deut 32:49 ( הַרנְֿבוֺ ), 34:1 ( id. ; all P), six miles west of Heshbon according to Onomastica (ed. Lag 283 ). Probably = modern Nebâ at northeast corner of Dead Sea, Survey E. Pal. i. 198 ff. GASm Geogr. 562 ff. Buhl Geogr. 266 f. Tristr Moab 318, 338 Merrill East of Jordan, 242 ff. — compare מִּסְגָּה . II. נְבוֺ proper name, of a divinity Nebo (loan-word in Hebrew, compare Phoenician proper name, masculine נבו ; = Assyrian Nabû , Schr COT Glossary and Isa 46:1 Jastr Rel. Babylonian 124 ff. Jen Kosmol. pass. Tiele Ass. u. Babylonian Geach. 532 f. Say Rel. Bab 112 ff. (compare Palmyrene proper name ברנבו נבוזבד, Vog Palm. No. 73 ), and this perhaps √ nabû , call, name , see נבא ); — Babylonian god נְבוֺ קֹרֵם בֵּל כָּרַע 46:1 .
